name: application-context-menu
title: Context Menu
description: Right-click menu with icon, shortcut, separator, and destructive-item support driven by a typed items prop contract.
useWhen: A surface (file, row, canvas item) has a set of contextual actions triggered by right-click or long-press.
You want a compact action list anchored to the pointer position rather than a fixed toolbar.
Grouping destructive actions (delete) visually apart from safe actions (copy, rename).
avoidWhen: The actions should always be visible — use a toolbar or button group instead.
Touch-only interfaces without a long-press affordance to trigger the menu.
There is only one action — a single button is simpler than a menu.
responsiveBehavior: The menu is absolutely positioned at a given x/y; clamp those coordinates to the viewport in your own event handler so the menu never renders off-screen.
accessibility: The menu uses role='menu' with role='menuitem' buttons so assistive tech announces it as a menu, not a generic list.
Destructive actions are marked with both color and a text label, not color alone.
Each item is a real <button>, so it is reachable and activatable via keyboard once focus enters the menu.

variants.title: Context Menu
variants.description: Right-click menu with icons, keyboard shortcut hints, a separator, and a destructive delete action.
accessibility: The destructive item uses red text and icon plus a visible label — never color as the only signal.

variants.title: Context Menu (Dark)
variants.description: Right-click menu adapted for dark surfaces with the same icon, shortcut, and destructive-item structure.
accessibility: Menu item text, icons, and the destructive red accent must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
